clue.text: City elegant in the past

parts.note: elegant means chic, stylish
something that happened in the past happened long ago

explanation.surface: A town that used to be stylish but has lost its sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicago is a large American metropolis on Lake Michigan, so it is an example of a city.

clue.text: Business propped up by a large amount in foreign currency

indicators.note: in a down clue, propped up by means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company, a business
a peck is an old dry measure, used loosely for a great deal

explanation.surface: A firm held up by a big sum in foreign money.
explanation.definitionFit: The copeck is a Russian coin, a hundredth of a rouble, so it is money from abroad.

clue.text: I am moving up, up to college — it's a sudden whim

parts.note: I am is contracted to I'm

indicators.note: in a down clue, moving up means the word written next is read from bottom to top

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics, a college of London University

explanation.surface: A student explains that heading up to university was an impulsive decision.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving up' turns the second UP into PU. LSE is the London School of Economics.
explanation.definitionFit: An impulse is a sudden urge to act without thinking, the same thing as a passing whim.

clue.text: Modern make-up employed by girl who married a son of Zeus?

definitions.text: Modern make-up employed by girl who married a son of Zeus?

indicators.note: employed by means held within, so the rearranged letters sit inside the name

parts.note: Ada is a girl's name

indicators.note: make-up suggests reassembly, so the letters of the word beside it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mythological bride wearing contemporary cosmetics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make-up' signals the rearranging and 'employed by' the holding inside. Read whole, the clue also describes the princess Perseus married, so the 'girl' does double duty in the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Andromeda was rescued from a sea monster by Perseus, son of Zeus, who then wed her.

clue.text: Public man Henry, poorly but past the worst

parts.note: overt means open, public
he is the pronoun for a man
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
poorly means ill

explanation.surface: A public figure called Henry is unwell but recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'past the worst' suggests recovery from illness, but the definition means past one's prime.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone past their prime, too old to perform at their best, is said idiomatically to be beyond the peak.

clue.text: Discern changes in reverse

indicators.note: changes tells us the letters of the word next to it are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone spots the alterations being made backwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' looks like part of the anagram signal, but it is the definition, used as a verb meaning to cancel a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: To reverse a decision or law is to revoke or annul it.

clue.text: To be found in Andorra — mountain sheep

indicators.note: to be found in tells us the letters are sitting inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A wild sheep living in the Andorran mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mountain sheep' looks like one phrase, but 'mountain' supplies the last letter of the run hidden across the dash.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is an uncastrated male sheep.

clue.text: Suffer the consequences when vehicles overturn

indicators.note: in a down clue, overturn means the word for vehicles is turned upside down, read bottom to top

parts.note: trams are passenger vehicles running on rails

explanation.surface: People pay the price when buses or trams tip over.
explanation.definitionFit: To smart is to feel a sting, as when suffering the penalty for something.

clue.text: Is artist, the Spanish one, a foreigner?

parts.note: taken as written
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
el is Spanish for the
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a Spanish painter counts as a foreigner.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of the Royal Academy of Arts in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of Israel is an example of a foreign national to a British solver.

clue.text: Lining up bandage

explanation.definitionFit: Dressing ranks is the military term for lining troops up straight; a dressing is also a covering applied to a wound.

clue.text: Fancy quires first sang in high voices

parts.note: to pipe is to sing or play in a shrill, high tone, so the past tense here
a ream is a quantity of paper made up of twenty quires

explanation.surface: Choirboys imagining the quires of music they first sang from as trebles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' is the noun, an idle notion. The clue says the quires come 'first', yet the paper measure ends the answer; the setter seems to mean PIPED is put in front of it, so read 'first' loosely.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, in the sense of an unrealistic hope or daydream, is an idle wish that will never come true.

clue.text: Characters in the lead in amateur golf relish exciting end to match

indicators.note: the characters in the lead of each word are their first letters, taken from the next five words

explanation.surface: An amateur golfer enjoys the thrilling finish to a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end to match' reads as the closing of the golf game, but 'end' is the last word giving its first letter, 'to' is a link, and 'match' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things that agree correspond or tally, which is what it means for them to match.

clue.text: About to get the measure of one of the strings

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about
an ell is an old measure of cloth length, about 45 inches
o' is the shortened form of of, as in o'clock or will-o'-the-wisp

explanation.surface: A musician is about to work out the length of one of the strings on an instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'strings' are not lengths of cord but the string section of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: The cello is a bowed instrument in the string family of the orchestra.

clue.text: A casual worker with long hair — Eve, perhaps

parts.note: a temp is a temporary worker taken on casually
a tress is a long lock of hair

explanation.surface: An agency worker with flowing locks is compared to Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: Eve tempted Adam with the forbidden fruit in Genesis, so she is a classic example of a seductress.

clue.text: Promotion of partnerships for the manufacture of lights

explanation.definitionFit: Arranging marriages or romantic pairings is matchmaking; making matches to strike for a flame is the other, literal sense.

clue.text: Chelsea leader left backs right in position for going through a gap in the wall

definitions.text: going through a gap in the wall

indicators.note: left means departed, so the letter named is taken away from the word for backs

parts.note: in football the backs make up the defence

indicators.note: the leader of the word Chelsea is its first letter
in tells us the letter for right goes inside the word for position

parts.note: a station is a post or position

explanation.surface: A football report on a Chelsea captain leaving and the backs moving to the right for a breach in the defensive wall.
explanation.walkthrough: The football picture misleads: 'left' means the Chelsea leader departs from the backs, giving DEFENE, and 'in' signals the insertion. The 'gap in the wall' is a window.
explanation.definitionFit: Defenestration is the act of throwing someone out of a window, and a window is an opening in a wall.

clue.text: A party to put restrictions on worship

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
to ration something is to restrict how much of it people get

explanation.surface: A group is told to limit its religious devotion.
explanation.definitionFit: Adoration is deep reverence or veneration, as in religious devotion.

clue.text: Complacent leader of gentlemen directed what gentlemen did

parts.note: smug means self-satisfied, complacent

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of the word gentlemen

parts.note: led means guided or directed

explanation.surface: A self-satisfied chief steering what gentlemen did.
explanation.walkthrough: In Kipling's 'A Smuggler's Song', the 'gentlemen' who go by at night are smugglers bringing in contraband.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's poem calls the contraband runners gentlemen, so the activity is illegal importing.

clue.text: Celebrate what you can do with a thing

parts.words: what you can do with a thing
parts.note: the phrase a thing can be rearranged into a night, so the answer's own instruction describes building a night from it

explanation.surface: Advice that any occasion can be turned into a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as an instruction: rearranging the letters of 'a thing' turns them into 'a night'.
explanation.definitionFit: To spend a whole evening enjoying yourself is an idiom for celebrating in style.

clue.text: In love, married serviceman subverted foreign government

indicators.note: subverted, literally turned from below, means in a down clue the whole run is read bottom to top

parts.note: nil, or love in tennis, means a score of nothing
erk is RAF slang for an aircraftman, a low-ranking serviceman

explanation.surface: A married soldier in love becomes a traitor to a foreign regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'subverted' reverses NIL, M and ERK together. ERK is British slang for a junior airman.
explanation.definitionFit: The Kremlin is the Moscow citadel, used to stand for the Russian government.

clue.text: Bill is singing well

explanation.definitionFit: An invoice is a bill for goods supplied; a singer in good voice is said to be performing well.

clue.text: Lethargic agent responsible for safeguarding general

indicators.note: safeguarding suggests protecting by surrounding, so one piece goes around the other

parts.note: a spy is a secret agent
Robert E. Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A drowsy secret agent is assigned to protect a general.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargic means sluggish and drowsy, wanting to doze.

clue.text: Irregular fighter is a thug, they say

indicators.note: they say tells us the word is identified by how it is pronounced

parts.note: gorilla is slang for a big brutish thug or heavy

explanation.surface: A soldier of an unofficial army is called a brute by his enemies.
explanation.definitionFit: A guerrilla is a member of an irregular force fighting outside a regular army.

clue.text: Material gathered by policemen on governor … 25 … is liable to result in prison

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: RUC is the Royal Ulster Constabulary, the former Northern Ireland police force
HE is His Excellency, the title of a governor

explanation.surface: Police and a governor share in a gathered fabric, a deed which could land someone in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was the police force of Northern Ireland until 2001. The clue runs on with an ellipsis into 25.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruche is a frill of pleated or gathered fabric used as trimming.

clue.text: Vanadium found in blue block

indicators.note: found in tells us one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: anil is the indigo plant and its blue dye
V is the chemical symbol for vanadium

explanation.surface: A metal discovered in a blue chunk of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: An anvil is the heavy iron block a blacksmith hammers metal on.

clue.text: Ring back about one shrub

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the reversed word goes round the letter for one
back tells us the word for ring is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them on the phone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A request to phone back about a single bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns CALL into LLAC, and 'about' puts it round I.
explanation.definitionFit: Lilac is a flowering bush with fragrant purple or white blossoms.

clue.text: Pan made Circe sit round one

indicators.note: round means placed around, so the rearranged letters surround the letter for one
made, as in made into something new, signals the letters are reworked

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: The enchantress of Greek myth is told to sit round one table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pan' looks like the Greek god beside Circe, but it is the verb meaning to slate. 'made' rearranges CIRCE SIT and 'round' wraps that around I.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a play or film is to condemn it harshly in a review.

clue.text: … is liable to result in prison

explanation.definitionFit: Can expresses possibility, being likely to happen; the can is also slang for jail.

clue.text: Debt-collector finally earning a long time in prison

parts.note: a dun is someone who demands payment of a debt

indicators.note: finally picks the final letter of the word earning

parts.note: an eon is an immensely long period of time

explanation.surface: A bailiff ends up spending years in jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A dungeon is a dark underground cell in a castle, so a kind of prison.

clue.text: With reddish hair greying patchily

indicators.note: patchily suggests something done unevenly, so the letters of the word beside it are jumbled

explanation.surface: A redhead whose colour is fading to grey in patches.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger is the colour of red-orange hair, so this adjective means tinged with that colour.
